# Cat The Mouse Company — Free 3D Cat & Mouse Game

> Cat The Mouse Company (https://catthemouse.co) is a free, mobile-first 3D browser game about cats catching mice. You start as a grey tabby and tap the mice that pop out of holes on a moonlit lawn; never go more than 5 seconds without a catch, or the round ends. Points from every round unlock six more cats — orange tabby, badger, black, white, calico and the tilcayo, the first new wild cat species described in over 100 years — and the yellow lizard, a new critter worth two mice. Formerly known as "Tilcayo Cat Game".

Last updated: 2026-10-01

## The game in brief

- Genre: arcade / reflex (whack-a-mole style). Free, no sign-up, no install; ad-supported, with an optional 50,000-point pack (US$ 3.44, Google sign-in required). Works on phones, tablets and desktop browsers.
- Clock: start with 5 s; each catch +0.8 s (capped at 5 s); empty slap −0.3 s.
- Porcupine and green snake: slapping them makes the cat lick its paw and stop hunting (2 s / 3 s). The snake eats mice that pop out right next to it.
- Lawn starts with 4 holes and a new one opens every 4.5 s until all 25 are dug; mice speed up smoothly.
- Shop: points buy cats — Orange Tabby 150,000, Badger 400,000, Black Cat 800,000, White Cat 1,400,000, Calico 2,200,000, Tilcayo 4,000,000 — and the Yellow Lizard (600,000, worth 2 mice). Your cat and lizard also appear in 1v1.
- Daily Challenge: catch 20 of the mouse of the day (one of 100 fancy mice), across any number of rounds that day, to add it to the album.
- Power-ups: Auto-catch (6 s), Full time (clock back to 5 s), Freeze (4 s: clock stopped, every critter frozen in ice).
- Hunter ranks: Sleepy Kitten 0, Curious Cub 5, Lawn Prowler 12, Night Hunter 20, Shadow Stalker 30, Lawn Legend 45, Mythic Mouser 65.
- Seals: 11, including streak seals for 5, 15, 60 and 90 days in a row.

## The tilcayo cat in brief

- Leopardus tilcayo Nogales-Ascarrunz, Aliaga-Rossel, Lescroart & Eizirik, 2026 — a tiger cat from the Bolivian Yungas cloud forest; first new wild cat species since the Pampas cat in 1923.
- Described in Lescroart et al., Current Biology (2026), doi:10.1016/j.cub.2026.08.059.
- About 45 cm head-to-body, 1.3 kg; rust-orange coat, large rosettes, two dark forehead stripes. One known individual, at Senda Verde Animal Refuge, Bolivia.
